_comment: net_session -- the two ORIGINAL netcode writers SB-NET and SB-BOOT could not except.
WHY A DOMAIN AT ALL FOR TWO FUNCTIONS. The ledger is not bookkeeping here, it is the thing
NET-SESSION's acceptance is written against: `reached by MIGRATION-LEDGER rows (state verified)
for both functions rather than by exceptions -- an exception entry for either is a failure of
this item, not a pass`. gen_writer_attribution.py reads EVERY tools/data/*_migration.json for its
derived half, so a row here is what makes the NET-SESSION scope disposable without an entry in
writer_dispositions.json. The alternative -- adding the two rows to somebody else's ledger --
would have put netcode bodies in the sim's or the AI's roster and made both domains' counts lie.
WHY THERE IS NO lockstep DOMAIN TO JOIN. The net/lockstep migration (RI-WIRE, RI-CUTOVER / C8)
predates the per-function ledger machinery and is tracked as tracker/reimpl.yaml items with
prose acceptance, not as generated rows. This profile does not retro-fit that work; its
membership query is deliberately NARROW -- gen_writer_attribution.owning_item() == NET-SESSION --
so it holds exactly the writers this item was opened for and empties itself if they are ever
re-attributed.
WHAT IT SHARES WITH THE REST OF THE CLOSURE: the namespace (mh::lockstep), the promotion key
([promote] lockstep -- these two joined that table, 31 seams -> 33), and turn_engine's install
accounting. What it does NOT share is the oracle: `netsessiontest` is its own suite because the
bodies are a boot-time store list and a frame function, neither of which the turn engine's
horizon/barrier fixture has any binding for.
ARMING IS UNAVAILABLE FOR BOTH, and that is measured rather than assumed:
session_globals_reset runs ONCE per process (llm_game_init_subsystems, WM_CREATE), so there is
no second call for a shadow arm to compare, and everything that boots afterwards consumes
what it wrote.
wait_screen_frame SENDS a CTL_RESYNC_END packet and DRAINS the socket. Shadow mode restores
state between arms; it can un-write a global and cannot un-send a datagram or un-consume a
stream, so an armed run would double the resume broadcast while reading clean.
The evidence is therefore the offline oracle plus the offline ADDRESS-TABLE check
(tools/check_net_session_addrs.py, fork F1B). It replaced a live read-back probe that ran in
BOTH configurations -- stock proving the address table, promoted proving our body -- and it is
strictly stronger: it proves all 22 rows non-vacuously where the live pair rested on 8, and it
runs in lint instead of needing two rig boots. The probe was deleted at fork F2F.
title: The lockstep session bootstrap and the leader resync frame

select.walk_why: The seeds ARE the answer, as in sim_resid and readers. Both bodies are complete functions named by DIRECT write attribution; a forward walk would add only Law-4 frontier leaves (mp_leave_reset_game_mode, time_resync_and_tick) and members of the lockstep closure this project already owns.

seeds.why: MEMBERSHIP FROZEN 2026-09-01: the domain is COMPLETE (both rows verified AND promoted -- the SIM-RESID-P wave's census refresh re-attributed the last NET-SESSION-routed writers to `ours`, so the original writer_attribution seed now legitimately resolves to nothing and would refuse). The original derivation is preserved in this note: every original writer of a region LIBMH WRITES that routed to item NET-SESSION via gen_writer_attribution.owning_item(); it produced exactly these two functions and the attribution ledger's history carries the routing.

paths._state_header_why: This domain's state interface is the module header itself: both bodies take their state and calls as parameters (session_init_state / wait_screen_state), which is what lets the oracle run them over plain locals with no game.

items._interface_why: The item owns its own interface -- there is no separate one to reuse, and the two structs live in the module header the bodies are declared in.

oracle._why: F1B (2026-09-12): the ADDRESS-TABLE half of this domain's evidence is no longer the live read-back. tools/check_net_session_addrs.py disassembles llm_net_session_globals_reset in the retail exe and requires its 28 absolute stores to fold into exactly the 22 region bases and constants net_session.h declares, under a sha256 stamp of the exe and the body -- offline, on every lint_repo run, with an extraction-totality arm that REFUSES rather than reporting a partial table. The probe (seams/net_session_probe.cpp) and tools/check_netprobe.py keep only the arm that needs a running process were DELETED at fork F2F (2026-09-12).
oracle._selftest_why: Its own suite, not lockstest's: these bodies are a boot-time store list and a frame function, and the turn engine's fixture binds neither the session globals nor the wait-screen state. The one place they DO meet -- the leader-vs-peer end-state comparison -- lives in lockstep_selftest.cpp, because the peer arm is the RX dispatcher and that file owns the crafted-packet harness.

rig._why: Neither member is armable (see the header), so the rig's role here was never a shadow run: it was the LIVE READ-BACK, and any run that booted the game at all produced the `[netprobe]` line -- which is why the cheapest single-peer launch is the mode. The probe was deleted at fork F2F and its evidence is now offline (check_net_session_addrs), so this domain needs no rig run at all; the mode is kept for the boot smoke it still gives.

rules.why: One batch, named exhaustively rather than by prefix: the two members share no prefix (one is llm_net_, the other llm_wait_) and a prefix rule broad enough to catch both would catch most of the netcode. Naming them makes a THIRD member -- a writer newly routed to this item -- fall to the default batch and be visible instead of silently absorbed.

_conductor_owned_why: The module header carries the shared structs AND the constant table the read-back probe compares against, so a writer editing it could move the body and the check together. turn_engine.cpp holds the promotion table and rx_dispatch.cpp the peer end of the shared transition -- both are edits ABOUT the closure rather than inside one body.
_non_autonomous_why: The item's own acceptance requires a design decision (splice vs translate for the resync half) and a live read-back run read by a human in two configurations. Neither is something the unattended loop should settle.
